instructions: Full-rank variational inference at d=390 requires an O(d²) dense Cholesky parameter vector that is computationally and memory-intractable. The radon model (d=390) is far above the threshold (d>30) where fullrank_vi becomes infeasible.
workflow:
Hard-exclusion category 8: fullrank_vi warmup for high-d models (radon, d=390).

Full-rank variational inference maintains a dense d×d covariance matrix parameterized via its Cholesky decomposition. This requires O(d²) parameters: at d=390, that is ~152,000 variational parameters. Computing the full Cholesky decomposition, storing the dense matrix, and running gradient steps on it becomes computationally and memory-intensive, making fullrank_vi impractical.

The hard threshold is d > 30: models above this dimension should not use fullrank_vi as a warmup. Excluded: radon (d=390), irt_2pl (d=144), stoch_vol (d=503), horseshoe (d=204), ill_cond_50 (d=50). Mean-field VI (meanfield_vi) remains available for all models (diagonal covariance, O(d) parameters), and for the small-d models (d <= 30), fullrank_vi can be tried.

Enabling fullrank_vi for radon would require either: (1) a reduced-rank approximation (e.g., factor-analysis VI with fixed rank r << d), or (2) a different warmup strategy designed for high-d (e.g., pathfinder, adapted-mclmc tuning). These are Phase 7 / v2 scope.

See RECIPE_GENERATION.md § Hard Exclusions Category 8 (lines 601-603) for the full context.
